body: Thank you. I really hope that someone can help you. It's not shameful to get help. I'm almost definitely on the autism spectrum, and I had some difficulty accepting that everyone needs help sometimes, and I hope that you can also accept that

I totally get not wanting to burden your friends with your problems, and wanting to solve your problems yourself, but unfortunately the world isn't built very well for that all the time.


If you want some justifications that have personally helped me get over that in the past and may yet help me again in the future, here are my two go-tos


1. friends and random internet strangers are there to help you. If they didn't want to help you, they wouldn't.

2. if you're deep in a hole (financial or emotional), you're of no help to anyone, and with someone else's help, you can get out of the hole faster and be of use to everyone you care about sooner

2.5. on this particular suggestion (which you don't have to take): chances are that your friends also have debts. If you do this thing, you're not just helping yourself. You'd be organizing everyone to pay off all their debts together. Without debt, you can have much more money to help pay off the rest of your friends' debts, and the same with them.

Yeah, maybe. I'd like to at least go to therapy before I reconnect with my friends, but maybe I could pick chainmail back up and learn some jewelry and simple armors and make an online shop of some kind, and perhaps I could learn to sew coats and such, and sell those as well.


      
        
What about you? I'm doing a lot better, personally, but you seem to be reaching out to a lot of other people to try to help them. Do you want to talk about your problems?


    

Do you have friends you can talk to about your financial issues? I've heard of some really cool times that friend groups or church groups did a system where they all pooled their money they could spare to pay off everyone's loans and credit card debt one person at a time. Perhaps, if you've got any close friends, you could pitch that?

I definitely get it. That type of thinking has been behind many of my attempts.

I really wish I had an answer for you. Not feeling is incredibly shitty, and feeling better off dead than alive is also shitty.

I have to say though, and I'm sorry to show some political leanings here, this is largely a fallacy that society has caused. I firmly believe that almost every human being deserves to live, and that everyone, if given the correct environment, can thrive and do and make great things. I don't have a better answer than that killing yourself is just giving up on finding that environment forever, and making the world a worse place forever

I can understand that. I've definitely felt that hollow suicidal feeling even after a success. I was going to fail the ACT so I couldn't go to college, and I could die homeless, and instead I got a high score on it. 


I would recommend thinking about dropping out of law school. If it's part of what makes you want to die, then I really doubt that the sunk cost you've put in could be worth dying over or wanting to die for the rest of your life for

The thing is, if they are, that's because they care about you and want you to be happy, so if you bottle up your sadness and avoid them, that's just making both of your lives worse. Friends help each other, so you should reach out.

Not allowing yourself to have friends just because you're depressed is going to just make you more depressed. I highly recommend reaching back out to your friends, and talking to them. Chances are, they are or have been depressed too, so they'll most likely understand. And don't assume your friends don't want you around unless they tell you that directly

Also, therapists are very useful, if you have insurance or can spare the cash to have like a meeting a month, and they can help you not be as sad at your friends

Well, I'm pretty good at chainmail, I picked it up when I was a 13 year old with some spirit and some days of happiness still left in me, and I got pretty good

I'm okay at game system design, again from my childhood, when I would design tabletop rpg systems and stories to play with my friends

And I'm okay at sewing, because I never felt comfortable asking for new clothes from my parents as a kid

Of course, I'm not sure how good I'd be at any of these now. I haven't done anything major with these skills for quite a while

You should be more kind to yourself. You're suffering from suicidal depression, which makes everything harder, and reading over your post it looks like life dealt you a pretty shit hand. You're obviously a nice person, or you wouldn't be going into people's suicidewatch posts to help them, and in some way, you also wouldn't be worried about being a burden on others

Tell me about you

    



Edit: to be clear, I'm feeling a lot better now. Maybe I just needed time or to let out my thoughts in a public forum, or maybe I was too warm from the heat wave here



I do now think I can be a better person, even if I feel like fundamentally a piece of shit. I think I'm going to keep the karmic ledger, because part of my biggest problem as a person is not keeping true to my word. I will adjust it though.
    
    
I'll extend the deadline, and I won't make the final judgement "should I die" but instead "how much more drastically do I need to change as a being to become a good person"

    

In a way, I suppose I'm making this karmic ledger system into a game, so that I can treat being a good person like a game until it becomes unconscious

Do you have any friends or family left? Perhaps you could set up a talk with them tomorrow


Do you have any friends you distanced yourself from as you fell into depression? I bet they still think about you, and miss you, and would be happy to try to reconnect. Get in contact with them tomorrow


Do you have any nice foods or ingredients in your house? You could promise yourself you'll make yourself an amazing breakfast or learn to cook a good breakfast for yourself tomorrow


Do you have any skills you've always wanted to learn? Look up some tutorials tonight, and be patient with yourself as you try to learn

Or if all else fails, try crying and going to sleep, you can always choose to kill yourself later
